### Start Buzz channel guided setup

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/channels/buzz.md

Launches the interactive setup wizard to configure a Buzz relay, account, and bot identity. Setup validates room access and persists configuration for Gateway operation.

```bash
openclaw channels add --channel buzz
```

--------------------------------

### Install and run the node host

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/plugins/google-meet.md

Install the Google Meet plugin and start the node host within the VM.

```bash
openclaw plugins install npm:@openclaw/google-meet
openclaw node run --host <gateway-host> --port 18789 --display-name parallels-macos
```

--------------------------------

### Install Dependencies and Start Dev Gateway Watcher

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/start/setup.md

Installs dependencies, performs initial setup, and starts the Gateway watch process in a named tmux session with hot reloading. Stops any active installed Gateway service before binding the port.

```bash
pnpm install
# First run only (or after resetting local OpenClaw config/workspace)
pnpm openclaw setup
pnpm gateway:watch
```

--------------------------------

### Install Docker and Docker Compose

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/hetzner.md

Installs prerequisites and Docker engine using the official setup script, then prints installed versions.

```bash
apt-get update
apt-get install -y git curl ca-certificates
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
docker --version
docker compose version
```

--------------------------------

### Start onboarding wizard with daemon installation

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/README.md

Runs onboarding after direct package installation with npm, pnpm, or Bun. Verifies model access, sets up the workspace, and configures the Gateway.

```bash
openclaw onboard --install-daemon
```

--------------------------------

### Run interactive LiteLLM onboarding in OpenClaw

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/providers/litellm.md

Starts the interactive setup process to authenticate OpenClaw with a LiteLLM API key.

```bash
openclaw onboard --auth-choice litellm-api-key
```

--------------------------------

### Launch Guided Channel Setup via Positional Argument or Flag

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/cli/channels.md

Open interactive setup directly for a specific channel using a positional argument or the `--channel` flag. Choosing back inside the wizard returns to the full channel selector.

```bash
openclaw channels add telegram
openclaw channels add --channel telegram
```

--------------------------------

### Run OpenClaw setup and repair assistant

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/web/tui.md

Start the assistant interactively, execute a single request, or apply automated configuration updates using `--yes`.

```bash
openclaw setup                       # start interactively
openclaw setup -m "status"           # run one request and exit
openclaw setup -m "set default model openai/gpt-5.2" --yes   # apply a config write
```

--------------------------------

### Start interactive channel setup

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/channels/qqbot.md

Runs the interactive channel configuration wizard. Provides an option for QR-code binding as an alternative to manually providing AppID and AppSecret.

```bash
openclaw channels add

```

--------------------------------

### Start local development server with pnpm ui:dev

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/web/control-ui.md

Launches a standalone local development server. Point the running UI at your Gateway WebSocket URL (such as `ws://127.0.0.1:18789`).

```bash
pnpm ui:dev
```

--------------------------------

### Start standalone mock preview with pnpm dev:ui:mock

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/web/control-ui.md

Launches an isolated preview environment populated with synthetic data and mock Gateway WebSocket responses on the designated port. Open the output URL in a fresh browser context without existing credentials.

```bash
pnpm dev:ui:mock -- --port 19321
```

--------------------------------

### GET /__openclaw__/assistant-media

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/web/control-ui.md

Checks availability and retrieves assistant local-media previews. Operators request metadata with a bearer token to obtain a short-lived media ticket, which is then used to render browser media.

```APIDOC
## GET /__openclaw__/assistant-media

### Description
Accesses assistant local-media previews using a two-step mechanism. Callers authenticate to obtain a scoped, short-lived media ticket via metadata, which is subsequently passed to render the media item.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/__openclaw__/assistant-media

### Parameters
#### Query Parameters
- **source** (string) - Required - The source path of the target local media file.
- **meta** (string) - Optional - Set to `1` when requesting media metadata and a short-lived scoped `mediaTicket`.
- **mediaTicket** (string) - Optional - Short-lived ticket scoped to the specific source path, used by browser-rendered media elements in place of gateway credentials.
```

--------------------------------

### Configure turn start parameters for Telegram direct codex message tool

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/test/fixtures/agents/prompt-snapshots/codex-runtime-happy-path/telegram-direct-codex-message-tool.md

Defines the initial runtime configuration, context values, sandbox policy, collaboration mode settings, and thread identification for a turn.

```json
{
  "additionalContext": {
    "openclaw_current_sender": {
      "kind": "untrusted",
      "value": "{\"sender\":{\"id\":\"1000001\",\"name\":\"Pash\",\"username\":\"pash\"}}"
    },
    "openclaw_temporal_context": {
      "kind": "application",
      "value": "## Temporal Context\nCurrent date: 2026-01-01\nTime zone: UTC\nFor the exact current time, use `session_status`."
    }
  },
  "approvalPolicy": "never",
  "approvalsReviewer": "user",
  "collaborationMode": {
    "mode": "default",
    "settings": {
      "developer_instructions": "# Collaboration Mode: Default\n\nYou are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.\n\nYour active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.\n\n## request_user_input availability\n\nUse the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.\n\nIn Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.\n\n## OpenClaw Agent Soul\n\nOpenClaw loaded these workspace instruction files from the active agent workspace. They are the canonical definitions of who you are, how you think and work, and the human you work alongside. Internalize and follow them accordingly.\n\n### /tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace/IDENTITY.md\n\n<IDENTITY.md contents will be here>\n\n### /tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace/SOUL.md\n\n<SOUL.md contents will be here>\n\n### /tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace/USER.md\n\n<USER.md contents will be here>",
      "model": "gpt-5.5",
      "reasoning_effort": "medium"
    }
  },
  "cwd": "/tmp/openclaw-happy-path/workspace",
  "effort": "medium",
  "input": [
    {
      "text": "<see Reconstructed Model-Bound Prompt Layers>",
      "text_elements": [],
      "type": "text"
    }
  ],
  "model": "gpt-5.5",
  "personality": "none",
  "sandboxPolicy": {
    "type": "dangerFullAccess"
  },
  "threadId": "thread-telegram-direct-codex-message-tool"
}
```

### GET /avatar/<agentId>

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/web/control-ui.md

Retrieves the avatar image or avatar metadata for a specific agent. When gateway authentication is enabled, requests require a valid gateway token.

```APIDOC
## GET /avatar/<agentId>

### Description
Retrieves the avatar image or avatar metadata for a specified agent. When gateway auth is configured, requests require a gateway bearer token.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/avatar/<agentId>

### Parameters
#### Path Parameters
- **agentId** (string) - Required - The unique identifier of the agent.

#### Query Parameters
- **meta** (string) - Optional - Set to `1` to return avatar metadata instead of the image binary.
- **v** (string) - Optional - Opaque revision used as a cache key for cache busting.
```

### Run guided onboarding setup

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/channels/clickclack.md

Launches the interactive onboarding flow to configure server URL, bot token, and workspace settings. A failed post-save verification check does not discard saved configuration.

```bash
openclaw onboard
```

### Quickstart with Peekaboo CLI

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/skills/peekaboo/SKILL.md

Basic commands to get started with Peekaboo, including checking permissions, listing applications, taking a screenshot, clicking an element, and typing text.

```bash
peekaboo permissions
peekaboo list apps --json
peekaboo see --annotate --path /tmp/peekaboo-see.png
peekaboo click --on B1
peekaboo type "Hello" --return
```

### Run onboarding setup in the container

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/podman.md

Launches the container in setup mode for initial onboarding. Access the UI at http://127.0.0.1:18789/ with the token generated in ~/.openclaw/.env.

```bash
./scripts/run-openclaw-podman.sh launch setup
```

### Recover npm install via installer script

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/updating.md

Runs global package installation directly via the installer to recover a partially updated npm install when `openclaw triage` cannot start.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --install-method npm
```

### Run Docker setup script

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/install/docker-vm-runtime.md

Initializes host directories, builds the local image, runs onboarding, generates a Gateway token, synchronizes configuration, and starts the container via Docker Compose.

```bash
./scripts/docker/setup.sh
```

```bash
sag voices
```


--------------------------------

### Run OpenClaw installer with --verbose flag

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/help/faq-first-run.md

Re-runs the installation script with `--verbose` to obtain detailed diagnostic feedback if the installer hangs. Examples include standard, beta, and git installation methods.

```bash
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --verbose
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --beta --verbose
curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --install-method git --verbose
```

--------------------------------

### Install Gateway using --wrapper flag

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/cli/gateway.md

Creates an executable wrapper script and supplies it via `--wrapper` during installation to launch Gateway through a secrets manager or helper.

```bash
cat > ~/.local/bin/openclaw-doppler <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
exec doppler run --project my-project --config production -- openclaw "$@"
EOF
chmod +x ~/.local/bin/openclaw-doppler

openclaw gateway install --wrapper ~/.local/bin/openclaw-doppler --force
openclaw gateway restart
```

Source: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/channels/tlon.md
